questions.q: Which major subject area in the Licensure Examination for Architects (LEA) covers the history of architecture, theory of architecture, and principles of planning?
o: History and Theory of Architecture; Principles of Planning and Urban Design
questions.n: This subject area integrates the evolution of design, theoretical frameworks, and the broader context of urban environments.

questions.q: Under Section 14 of RA 9266, which subject area focuses on technical aspects like structural systems and building materials?
o: Structural Design, Building Materials, and Methods of Construction
questions.n: This cluster covers the physical realization of buildings, ensuring they are stable and utilize appropriate technologies.

questions.q: Which subject area tests the candidate's ability to translate a design program into a physical layout, focusing on spatial relationships?
questions.n: This is the core design component where candidates demonstrate their ability to organize spaces and sitework.

questions.q: Section 14 mandates that the BoA must submit examination results to the PRC within how many days after the last day of the exam?
questions.n: The law provides a 30-day window for the results to be processed and submitted to the commission.

questions.q: Which subject area specifically covers the laws, ethics, and standards that govern an architect's professional conduct?
o: Professional Practice, Ethics, Laws, and Regulations
questions.n: This area encompasses all the legalities, including RA 9266, the NBC, and the Architect's Code of Ethics.

questions.q: What is the legal term for the 'binding strategy' consisting of drawings, specifications, and other documents signed and sealed by the architect?
questions.n: This legal term encompasses all professional outputs produced by the architect as part of their service agreement.

questions.q: According to Section 3 of RA 9266, what is a 'Consulting Architect'?
o: An RLA with exceptional expertise or specialization in a branch of architecture
A foreign architect practicing under an STP
A junior architect assisting a principal
An architect-of-record who signs the permit
questions.n: Consultants are recognized for their advanced knowledge in specific areas like acoustics, lighting, or heritage.

questions.q: How does RA 9266 define 'Architecture' in Section 3?
o: The technical drawing of floor plans and elevations
The business of designing structures for profit
The art and science of erecting buildings
The planning, designing, and constructing of buildings in their totality with regard to environment and principles of utility, strength, and beauty
questions.n: This definition incorporates the Vitruvian triad (utilitas, firmitas, venustas) and environmental context.

questions.q: What is the term for the 'Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects' (IAPOA) currently recognized by the BoA?
questions.n: The UAP is the only organization currently recognized by the PRC and BoA as the IAPOA for architects.

questions.q: What does the term 'Service Agreement' refer to in Section 3 of RA 9266?
o: A receipt for professional services rendered
An oral agreement between client and architect
A notarized written contract stipulating scope of services and compensation
A project brief provided by the owner
questions.n: This document serves as the legal basis for the professional relationship and fee structure.

questions.q: Under Section 4, how many members comprise the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture?
o: Three (3) Members (A chairman and two members)
questions.n: The board consists of three RLAs who oversee the regulation of the profession.

questions.q: Who has the power to appoint the members of the PRBOA from a list of nominees submitted by the PRC?
questions.n: As with all professional regulatory boards, the members are presidential appointees.

questions.q: To be a member of the PRBOA, an architect must have been in active practice for at least how many years?
questions.n: A decade of active practice is required to ensure the member has deep professional maturity.

questions.q: What is the 'Term of Office' for a member of the PRBOA?
o: Three (3) years (with one reappointment for 3 more years)
questions.n: A member serves a 3-year term and can be reappointed once, for a total maximum of 6 years.

questions.q: According to Section 7, which body provides administrative assistance (secretariat) to the PRBOA?
o: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
questions.n: The PRC serves as the umbrella agency providing logistics, records, and staff support for all boards.

questions.q: What is the required minimum width for a Tactile Surface Indicator (Warning Block) at ramps or stairs?
questions.n: This width ensures that PWDs with visual impairments can feel the texture change well before the elevation change.

questions.q: In the latest standards, what is the required maximum height for Elevator Buttons from the floor level?
questions.n: This height ensures that all buttons are within the reach of individuals in a seated position.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width for a sidewalk or walkway to be considered accessible under BP 344?
questions.n: 1.20m is the legal minimum, though 1.50m is standard for two wheelchairs to pass each other.

questions.q: What are the minimum dimensions for an accessible elevator car?
questions.n: This size allows a wheelchair to enter and have enough depth for the user and an attendant.

questions.q: In an accessible toilet, what is the required distance of the Grab Bar center from the water closet centerline?
questions.n: This distance allows the user to have adequate leverage while sitting or transferring.

questions.q: Within how many days must the Building Official issue the Building Permit after payment of fees?
questions.n: The NBC mandates that permits be issued within 15 days if all plans are compliant and fees are paid.

questions.q: What is the 'Validity of a Building Permit' if construction does not commence?
questions.n: A Building Permit is valid for 12 months; if work hasn't started by then, it expires.

questions.q: If construction work is suspended, the permit becomes void if the suspension lasts for how many days?
questions.n: The permit is voided if work is abandoned or suspended for a total of 120 days.

questions.q: Under the National Building Code, what is 'Type V Construction'?
questions.n: Type V is the most durable and fire-resistive classification in the code.

questions.q: Who is legally responsible for the 'Entry and Inspection' of buildings to ensure compliance with the NBC?
questions.n: The Building Official has the legal authority to enter premises to verify adherence to the National Building Code.
